grh_8d574689b880d3eb8dab.title: General Guilford's Widow
paragraphs: Britt becomes lost near Minton and meets Hannah Guilford, widow of celebrated General William Guilford, who insists that her husband is still alive despite the monument honoring his death with his regiment five years earlier. Britt discovers that the general really has been hiding in the house: illness had taken him away from his command just before a Cheyenne attack wiped out his men, and when he returned home to find himself praised as a dead hero he was too afraid of a court-martial or accusations of desertion to reveal the truth. Hannah has sacrificed five years protecting the secret, but finally refuses to continue when Guilford threatens Britt rather than face the consequences. The general dies moments later, and a fire destroys the house with his body inside; Britt allows the public to keep its heroic version of Guilford's death while Hannah is finally able to begin a new life.

The cast includes Jimmy Stewart, [[person|virginia-gregg|Virginia Gregg]], [[person|parley-baer|Parley Baer]], Robert Griffin, and James Stewart. Other credited names include Jack Johnstone as director and John Wald as announcer.
The surviving recording runs about 30 minutes. Characters credited in this version include [[character|Britt Ponset]].

grh_8dcbbace22af857895fb.title: Out in Colorado
paragraphs: Labor organizer Mother Mary Jones enters the Colorado mining strike zone despite orders barring her from Trinidad and is repeatedly arrested for refusing to stay away from the striking miners and their families. General Chase and the state militia try deportation, confinement and intimidation, but Jones treats every arrest as another chance to expose the power being used against workers; even after weeks held in isolation, she continues writing and challenging the soldiers guarding her. Released and warned never to return, she instead heads to Washington to testify before the House Mines and Mining Committee about conditions in Colorado. While she is there, the Ludlow Massacre destroys the miners' tent colony and kills women and children. The strike is lost, but the drama closes by placing that defeat within the longer labor struggle Jones continues for the rest of her life.

The broadcast is also associated with [[org|org.9b0a0ccffce2f7d3|Sears, Roebuck and Company]].
